Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 8:5: The second refining is in his fulfillment of all 248 positive commandments of the Torah and of the words of the Rabbis, and especially in setting fixed times for Torah study, and in praying with intention, and in Grace after Meals and in all the blessings over pleasure with intention, and in loving every single Jew as the apple of his own eye, and in honoring the Sabbath in all its particulars; and each night he should rise after midnight to mourn over Jerusalem and to occupy himself with Torah, and all his deeds should be for the sake of Heaven, out of love:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 8:6: The third refining is at the time he prepares himself to be sanctified with the Holy Spirit:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 8:7: The fourth is in the purification of the body through immersion and clean garments:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 8:8: The fifth is at the time he prepares himself to receive the Holy Spirit, after all the good character traits have become implanted in him as a fixed acquisition: he should enter a room alone, having immersed and in holiness, in a place where the voices of people and the chirping of birds will not disturb him; and if it is after midnight, this is more fitting for everything. He should close his eyes and strip his thought of all matters of this world, as though his soul had left him, like one who is dead and feels nothing at all. Afterward he should exert and strengthen himself with a powerful longing to reflect upon the supernal world and to cleave there to the roots of his soul and to the supernal lights, and he should imagine to himself as though his soul had left him and ascended above, and he should depict the supernal worlds as though he were standing within them.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 8:9: And if he has performed some unification, he should reflect upon it, in order to draw down through it light and abundance to all the worlds, and he should intend to receive his own portion of it as well, at the end; and he should be still in thought, as though the spirit had rested upon him, for a certain measure of time. And if he feels nothing at all, it appears that he is not yet fit and ready, and he should therefore strengthen himself still further, from then on, in service and holiness, and after some days return to seclude himself in the manner mentioned, until he merits and the spirit rests upon him:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 8:10: And when it does come upon him, he must discern whether he is still not pure and clean, and this spirit may be the sitra achra (the Other Side), or at the very least a mixture of evil with good — and the incident of Ben Azzai and Ben Zoma (Chagigah 14b) in their ascent to the Pardes proves this. And this is tested by what is revealed to him: whether all his words are true, or whether truth and falsehood are mixed, or whether his words concern idle matters of the vanities of this world, or matters not in accordance with the Torah, and the like — for then he must push it away from himself, and also strengthen himself more and more in service, until all his words become trustworthy and imbued with the fear of Heaven, and so on:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 8:11: And know that at first the spirit will come upon him only occasionally, at distant intervals, and also that the matters will be minor and not profound, and also that his words will be few, and as he continues, his power will grow stronger in all the particulars mentioned. Now the sum of the whole matter is the refining of the material to the very last degree, and the uprooting of the musings of thought and the imaginative faculty within him entirely, and cleaving to the supernal beings in the utmost attachment. And you must reflect on everything we wrote in Part One, Gate Six, for there the order of the conduct of piety is explained at greater length:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 4 1:1-3: On the modes of practice for attaining the Holy Spirit:

We have already explained in Part Three, Gate Seven, that there are five modes of attainment: the Holy Spirit, the souls of the righteous, angels called maggidim, Elijah of blessed memory, and the dream.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 4 1:4: And each one of these can possibly be attained of itself, through a person's holiness and his engagement in Torah, without the need for any other deed. It is also possible to attain them through a particular deed, once it has first been established that the person is fit and prepared for the attainment. And this second matter will be explained in this part, from everything found written in the books of the early sages.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 4 1:5: And it divides into three gates. The first, on the modes of the deeds; the second, on the mode of attainment; the third, on the conditions for attainment. And I have already written in my great book called Etz Chaim several unifications and wondrous kinds of ways concerning the matter of attainment, and if the blessed Name so decrees, I shall write them out clearly in a part by itself:
